questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The sun ___ in the east.
questions.explanation: A universal truth is stated in the simple present, with -s for a singular subject.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Ria ___ a letter at this moment.
questions.explanation: 'At this moment' needs the present continuous: is writing.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: My father ___ in this office since 2012.
questions.explanation: 'Since' with a past starting point and a continuing action takes the present perfect.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: She ___ the cake before the guests came.
questions.explanation: The baking was completed before another past action, so the past perfect is used.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Next week at this time, we ___ on a beach in Goa.
questions.explanation: An action in progress at a future time uses the future continuous.

questions.q: Which sentence uses the correct tense?
options: She has gone there last week.
They have lived here for years.
questions.explanation: The present perfect cannot be used with a finished time like 'yesterday', and 'know' is not used in the continuous.

questions.q: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb in brackets: 'The train ___ (leave) before I reached the platform.'
questions.explanation: The train's departure happened before my arrival, so the past perfect is used.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'He has gone to Delhi last month.'
questions.answer: He went to Delhi last month.
questions.explanation: A finished time expression requires the simple past.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The boys ___ cricket every evening.
questions.explanation: A plural subject takes the plural simple present verb: play.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: My friend ___ in Chennai.
questions.explanation: A singular subject takes lives.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: All of the milk ___ spilt.
questions.explanation: 'Milk' is uncountable, so the verb is singular: was.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Both of my brothers ___ engineers.
questions.explanation: 'Both' is plural, so it takes 'are'.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The woman as well as her children ___ safe.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' does not change the number of the subject, which is 'woman'.

questions.q: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: The trousers is in the cupboard.
A bunch of keys was found on the road.
questions.explanation: The subject 'bunch' is singular, so the verb is 'was'.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'The list of items are on the desk.'
questions.answer: The list of items is on the desk.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with 'list', not with 'items'.

questions.q: Complete and explain: 'Two-thirds of the apples ___ rotten.'
questions.answer: are. A fraction takes its verb from the noun after 'of', and 'apples' is plural.
keyPoints: verb agrees with the noun after 'of'
questions.explanation: With fractions, the noun that follows decides the verb.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: My mother bought ___ umbrella.
questions.explanation: 'Umbrella' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: She has ___ unique collection of stamps.
questions.explanation: 'Unique' begins with a 'yoo' sound, a consonant sound, so 'a' is used.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: ___ Indian Ocean lies to the south of India.
questions.explanation: Names of oceans take the definite article.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: I have ___ friends in this city, so I feel at home.
questions.explanation: 'Friends' is countable and plural, so 'many' is used.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: There is very ___ sugar in my tea; it tastes bitter.
questions.explanation: 'Sugar' is uncountable, and 'very little' means hardly any.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: The honesty is the best policy.
I need an hour to finish the work.
questions.explanation: 'Hour' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is correct; the other sentences misuse articles.

questions.q: Fill in with a, an or the: 'He is ___ best player in ___ team.'
questions.explanation: Superlatives take 'the'.

questions.q: Explain why 'the' is used in 'The poor need our help.'
questions.answer: 'The' before an adjective such as 'poor' makes it refer to a whole class of people, here all poor people, and the phrase takes a plural verb.
keyPoints: the + adjective names a class of people
questions.explanation: This construction turns an adjective into a group noun.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: The teacher divided the sweets ___ the twenty children.
questions.explanation: 'Among' is used for more than two persons or things.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: She came to school ___ foot.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'on foot'.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: Mr. Das has been teaching here ___ twenty years.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a period of time.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: I prefer tea ___ coffee.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' is followed by 'to', not 'than'.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: He worked hard ___ he could pass the examination.
questions.explanation: 'So that' introduces a purpose.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: The verb 'insist' takes the preposition 'on'.

questions.q: Combine using 'because': 'He was absent. He was ill.'
questions.answer: He was absent because he was ill.
questions.explanation: 'Because' joins an effect with its cause.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks with prepositions: 'She was angry ___ me ___ forgetting her book.'
questions.explanation: We are angry with a person and for something done.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ ride a bicycle when I was six.
questions.explanation: 'Could' expresses ability in the past.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ I come in, sir?
questions.explanation: 'May I' is used to ask for permission.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: He ___ be at home; his car is outside.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses a logical conclusion from evidence.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ you like some more rice?
questions.explanation: 'Would you like...?' is the polite way to make an offer.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: Students ___ keep silence in the library.
questions.explanation: 'Should' expresses duty or what is expected.

questions.q: Which sentence shows a prohibition?
options: You must not enter this room.
You need not enter this room.
questions.explanation: 'Must not' forbids an action.

questions.q: Rewrite using 'can': 'She is able to solve the problem.'
keyPoints: base form of the verb follows
questions.explanation: 'Is able to' and 'can' both express ability.

questions.q: Explain why 'He can swims' is wrong and write the correct sentence.
questions.answer: A modal verb is followed by the base form of the verb, with no -s. The correct sentence is 'He can swim.'
questions.explanation: Modal verbs do not change form for the third person.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The song ___ by the children.
questions.explanation: The passive of the simple past is was + past participle (sung).

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Letters ___ by the postman every day.
questions.explanation: A plural subject in the simple present passive takes 'are + past participle'.

questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'He had written a letter.'
options: A letter was written by him.
A letter had been written by him.
A letter has been written by him.
A letter is written by him.
questions.explanation: Past perfect active becomes had been + past participle.

questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'Do you know him?'
options: Does he be known to you?
questions.explanation: Simple present questions become 'Is/Are + subject + past participle', and 'know' usually takes 'to'.

questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'She will sing a song.'
options: A song will be sung by her.
A song will sung by her.
A song would be sung by her.
A song is sung by her.
questions.explanation: Future passive: will be + past participle.

questions.q: Which sentence is in the active voice?
options: The farmers grow rice in Punjab.
questions.explanation: In 'The farmers grow rice' the subject performs the action.

questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'The gardener waters the plants every morning.'
questions.answer: The plants are watered by the gardener every morning.
questions.explanation: Simple present passive is is/are + past participle.

questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'People say that honesty is the best policy.'
questions.answer: It is said that honesty is the best policy.
questions.explanation: Sentences with 'say that' often take the passive form 'It is said that'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, 'I live in Pune.'
options: She said that she lived in Pune.
She said that I lived in Pune.
She said that she would live in Pune.
She said that she had live in Pune.
questions.explanation: The present tense becomes the past, and 'I' becomes 'she'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I can swim.'
options: He said that I could swim.
He said that he would swim.
He said that he could swim.
He said that he can to swim.
questions.explanation: 'Can' changes to 'could' and 'I' to 'he'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, 'My brother is coming today.'
options: She said that my brother was coming that day.
She said that her brother had come that day.
She said that her brother would come the next day.
She said that her brother was coming that day.
questions.explanation: 'My' becomes 'her', 'is coming' becomes 'was coming', and 'today' becomes 'that day'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said to her, 'Are you ready?'
options: He asked her that she was ready.
He asked her if she was ready.
He asked her was she ready.
He asked her what she was ready.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'if', in statement order.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: The mother said to the child, 'Please sit down.'
options: The mother said to the child that please sit down.
The mother requested the child that sit down.
The mother requested the child to sit down.
The mother asked the child sit down.
questions.explanation: A polite request is reported with 'requested ... to + verb'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: Rahul said, 'Hurrah! We have won the match.'
options: Rahul exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
Rahul exclaimed with joy that we had won the match.
Rahul exclaimed with sorrow that they had won the match.
Rahul exclaimed with joy that they would win the match.
questions.explanation: 'Hurrah' shows joy; 'we' becomes 'they' and the present perfect becomes the past perfect.

questions.q: Change into indirect speech: Seema said to me, 'I will help you.'
questions.answer: Seema told me that she would help me.
keyPoints: pronouns change: I to she, you to me
questions.explanation: Reporting changes the tense and the pronouns.

questions.q: Change into direct speech: She asked him whether he had seen her bag.
questions.answer: She said to him, 'Have you seen my bag?'
keyPoints: question order restored with a question mark
he becomes you, her becomes my, had seen becomes have seen
questions.explanation: A reported yes/no question becomes a direct question with inverted word order.

questions.q: Which of these is a coordinating conjunction?
questions.explanation: 'But' joins two clauses of equal rank; the others introduce subordinate clauses.

questions.q: Which of these is a complex sentence?
options: I did not go because it was raining.
questions.explanation: It has a main clause and a subordinate clause beginning with 'because'.

questions.q: Combine using a relative pronoun: 'The man is my uncle. He lives next door.'
options: The man who is my uncle who lives next door.
The man which lives next door is my uncle.
The man whom lives next door is my uncle.
The man who lives next door is my uncle.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject of 'lives' and refers to a person.

questions.q: Change the degree: 'Iron is the most useful metal.'
options: Iron is as useful as any other metal.
Iron is more useful than any other metal.
Iron is the more useful than other metal.
Iron is useful than any metal.
questions.explanation: The superlative is rewritten as a comparative with 'than any other'.

questions.q: Rewrite in the negative form: 'Everyone likes ice cream.'
questions.explanation: 'Nobody dislikes' keeps the original meaning in a negative form.

questions.q: Which sentence contains a noun clause?
options: I do not know where she lives.
The girl who lives here is kind.
Because he was late, he was scolded.
questions.explanation: 'Where she lives' is the object of 'know' and so acts as a noun.

questions.q: Change into an assertive sentence: 'Who can doubt his honesty?'
questions.answer: No one can doubt his honesty.
questions.explanation: A rhetorical 'Who can...?' means 'No one can...'.

questions.q: Combine using a participle: 'She finished her work. She went out to play.'
questions.answer: Having finished her work, she went out to play.
questions.explanation: A participle phrase shows that one action was completed before the other.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: A direct question ends with a question mark and begins with a capital letter.

questions.q: Which sentence has correct capital letters?
questions.explanation: The first word of a sentence and the name of a city begin with capitals.

questions.q: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
options: Delhi, the capital of India, is a big city.
Delhi the capital, of India is a big city.
Delhi, the capital of India is, a big city.
Delhi the capital of India, is a big city.
questions.explanation: Commas enclose a phrase that adds extra information.

questions.q: Choose the correct possessive form: The ___ playground is closed.
questions.explanation: 'Children' is an irregular plural not ending in s, so 's is added.

questions.q: Which sentence uses hyphens correctly?
questions.explanation: The compound noun is written sister-in-law with two hyphens.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: The exclamation mark goes inside the quotation marks, and the speaker tag begins with a small letter.

questions.q: Punctuate correctly: the boy asked his mother may i go out to play
questions.answer: The boy asked his mother, 'May I go out to play?'
keyPoints: capital letters for The and May
inverted commas and a question mark
questions.explanation: The spoken question is placed in inverted commas and ends with a question mark.

questions.q: Insert the missing commas: My teacher Mr Rao who is very strict gave us extra homework.
questions.answer: My teacher, Mr Rao, who is very strict, gave us extra homework.
keyPoints: commas around the name Mr Rao
commas around the clause who is very strict
questions.explanation: Commas set off extra information that can be removed without changing the main sentence.

questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'begin'.
questions.explanation: 'Begin' and 'start' have the same meaning.

questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'brave'.
questions.explanation: A brave person is fearless; a cowardly person is full of fear.

questions.q: What is a person who travels on foot called?
questions.explanation: A pedestrian walks along roads rather than travelling in a vehicle.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Separate' has an 'a' after the p: sep-a-rate.

questions.q: The prefix 'mis-' in 'misunderstand' means
questions.explanation: 'Mis-' means wrongly or badly.

questions.q: If a person is 'reluctant' to speak, he is
questions.explanation: 'Reluctant' means unwilling or hesitant.

questions.q: Write the plural forms of 'child', 'tooth' and 'sheep'.
questions.explanation: These are irregular plurals.

questions.q: Explain the difference between 'principal' and 'principle', with a sentence for each.
questions.answer: 'Principal' means the head of a school (or main): The principal addressed us. 'Principle' means a rule or belief: Honesty is a good principle.
keyPoints: principal = head of a school or chief
questions.explanation: The words sound alike but differ in meaning.

questions.q: What does the idiom 'break a leg' mean when said before a performance?
questions.explanation: It is a way of wishing a performer good luck.

questions.q: What does the idiom 'it is raining cats and dogs' mean?
options: Animals are falling from the sky.
questions.explanation: The idiom means heavy rain.

questions.q: What does the idiom 'to call it a day' mean?
options: to stop working for the day
questions.explanation: It means to stop doing something, usually work, for the time being.

questions.q: What does 'the black sheep of the family' mean?
options: a person who is seen as a disgrace to the family
questions.explanation: The black sheep is a member who is regarded as a failure or disgrace.

questions.q: What does the phrasal verb 'carry out' mean in 'The doctors carried out the test'?
questions.explanation: 'Carry out' means to do or perform a task.

questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The hikers had to ___ the climb because of the storm.
questions.explanation: 'Give up' means to abandon an effort.

questions.q: Explain the idiom 'to add fuel to the fire' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: It means to make a bad situation worse: His angry reply only added fuel to the fire.
keyPoints: means to worsen a difficult situation
questions.explanation: The idiom compares making things worse to feeding a fire.

questions.q: Explain the phrasal verb 'run out of' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: 'Run out of' means to have no more of something: We ran out of milk this morning.
questions.explanation: It is used when a supply is finished.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Ladakh is a cold desert high in the mountains. It receives very little rain, and winter temperatures can fall far below freezing. Even so, farmers there grow barley and apricots, using water from melting glaciers carried through narrow channels to their fields.' What do farmers in Ladakh grow, according to the passage?
questions.explanation: The last sentence names barley and apricots.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Ladakh is a cold desert high in the mountains. It receives very little rain, and winter temperatures can fall far below freezing. Even so, farmers there grow barley and apricots, using water from melting glaciers carried through narrow channels to their fields.' Where do the farmers get water for their fields?
questions.explanation: They use glacier water carried through channels.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Ladakh is a cold desert high in the mountains. It receives very little rain, and winter temperatures can fall far below freezing. Even so, farmers there grow barley and apricots, using water from melting glaciers carried through narrow channels to their fields.' Why is Ladakh described as a 'cold desert'?
options: It is cold and receives very little rain
It is full of sand dunes
questions.explanation: A desert gets very little rain; Ladakh also has freezing winters.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Ladakh is a cold desert high in the mountains. It receives very little rain, and winter temperatures can fall far below freezing. Even so, farmers there grow barley and apricots, using water from melting glaciers carried through narrow channels to their fields.' How do Ladakh's farmers manage to grow crops despite the harsh climate?
questions.answer: They bring water from melting glaciers through narrow channels to their fields and grow crops such as barley and apricots.
keyPoints: grow hardy crops like barley and apricots
questions.explanation: Channelling glacier meltwater makes up for the lack of rain.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'The old clock in the village square had stopped years ago, but nobody had bothered to repair it. One day, a young boy named Imran climbed the tower with a small toolbox. After two days of patient work, the hands began to move again. People gathered below and cheered, and the first chime rang out across the fields.' Who repaired the clock?
questions.explanation: The boy named Imran did the repair.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'The old clock in the village square had stopped years ago, but nobody had bothered to repair it. One day, a young boy named Imran climbed the tower with a small toolbox. After two days of patient work, the hands began to move again. People gathered below and cheered, and the first chime rang out across the fields.' How long did Imran take to repair the clock?
questions.explanation: The passage says he worked for two days.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'The old clock in the village square had stopped years ago, but nobody had bothered to repair it. One day, a young boy named Imran climbed the tower with a small toolbox. After two days of patient work, the hands began to move again. People gathered below and cheered, and the first chime rang out across the fields.' What does 'patient work' tell us about Imran?
options: He worked carefully without giving up
questions.explanation: Patient work over two days shows steady effort.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'The old clock in the village square had stopped years ago, but nobody had bothered to repair it. One day, a young boy named Imran climbed the tower with a small toolbox. After two days of patient work, the hands began to move again. People gathered below and cheered, and the first chime rang out across the fields.' How did the villagers react when the clock started again?
questions.answer: They gathered below the tower and cheered.
questions.explanation: The passage states their reaction directly.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'The Great Indian bustard is a large bird found in dry grasslands. Its numbers have fallen sharply because its grassland habitat has been turned into farms, and because power lines in its path are dangerous. Conservation groups are protecting nesting areas and marking power lines so that birds can see them.' Where is the Great Indian bustard found?
questions.explanation: The first sentence says dry grasslands.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'The Great Indian bustard is a large bird found in dry grasslands. Its numbers have fallen sharply because its grassland habitat has been turned into farms, and because power lines in its path are dangerous. Conservation groups are protecting nesting areas and marking power lines so that birds can see them.' Which threat to the bird is mentioned?
questions.explanation: Its habitat has been turned into farms.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'The Great Indian bustard is a large bird found in dry grasslands. Its numbers have fallen sharply because its grassland habitat has been turned into farms, and because power lines in its path are dangerous. Conservation groups are protecting nesting areas and marking power lines so that birds can see them.' Why are power lines being marked?
options: So that birds can see them and avoid them
questions.explanation: The passage states the purpose: birds can see them.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'The Great Indian bustard is a large bird found in dry grasslands. Its numbers have fallen sharply because its grassland habitat has been turned into farms, and because power lines in its path are dangerous. Conservation groups are protecting nesting areas and marking power lines so that birds can see them.' Name two causes of the fall in numbers and one step taken to help the bird.
questions.answer: Causes: grassland turned into farms and dangerous power lines. Step: protecting nesting areas (or marking power lines).
keyPoints: protecting nesting areas or marking power lines
questions.explanation: The passage lists both causes and the conservation steps.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kavya's school bus broke down halfway to the museum. While the driver called for help, the teacher suggested a game: each student had to describe the museum they imagined. By the time a new bus arrived, the children had spoken about robots, dinosaurs and ancient coins, and nobody was grumbling about the delay.' What happened to the school bus?
questions.explanation: The bus broke down halfway.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kavya's school bus broke down halfway to the museum. While the driver called for help, the teacher suggested a game: each student had to describe the museum they imagined. By the time a new bus arrived, the children had spoken about robots, dinosaurs and ancient coins, and nobody was grumbling about the delay.' What did the teacher suggest?
options: A game of describing an imagined museum
questions.explanation: The teacher proposed that each student describe the museum they imagined.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kavya's school bus broke down halfway to the museum. While the driver called for help, the teacher suggested a game: each student had to describe the museum they imagined. By the time a new bus arrived, the children had spoken about robots, dinosaurs and ancient coins, and nobody was grumbling about the delay.' What does the passage suggest about the teacher's idea?
options: It kept the children cheerful during the wait
questions.explanation: Nobody grumbled about the delay, so the game worked.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kavya's school bus broke down halfway to the museum. While the driver called for help, the teacher suggested a game: each student had to describe the museum they imagined. By the time a new bus arrived, the children had spoken about robots, dinosaurs and ancient coins, and nobody was grumbling about the delay.' How did the children spend the time while waiting?
questions.answer: They played a game in which each described an imagined museum, talking about robots, dinosaurs and ancient coins.
questions.explanation: The passage describes the game and what the children said.
